newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli tax revenues unchanged in three months.
newsitem.headline: Israeli tax revenues unchanged in three months.

text.p: Israeli government revenues from taxes and fees reached 25.3 billion shekels in the three months ended on February 28, unchanged in real terms from a year earlier, the Treasury said on Tuesday.
After taking into account changes in the tax code, revenues were 0.7 percent lower after inflation in the three months.

The Treasury did not release separate figures for February, but on Monday it reported that the budget deficit for February had fallen to 561 million shekels in the month from 1.41 billion shekels in January.

The Treasury said revenues from income and property tax rose one percent after inflation from a year ago to 13.6 billion shekels in the three months. It said income tax revenues rose a real seven percent while property tax revenues slumped a real 32 percent.

Revenues from customs and the value-added tax fell one percent after inflation to 11.1 billion shekels in the period, it said. The Treasury attributed the drop to a sharp decline in customs revenues from the imports of consumer durables.
